raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose
On Jetson AGX Thor (SM110), the QSA top-k dispatcher selects `cooperative_topk` because SM110 satisfies `has_device_capability(90)`. The cooperative kernel requests a 16-block cluster, but Thor supports a maximum cluster dimension of eight, causing model warmup to fail.

Exclude SM110 from the cooperative path so it uses the existing `persistent_topk` fallback.

## Test Plan
Manually reproduced the cooperative top-K launch failure on Jetson AGX Thor (SM110) on Qwen3.8 Next Flash and verified successful server startup and inference with the persistent top-K fallback.


---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

</details>

We hit this on Jetson AGX Thor (SM 11.0) in nightly CI, serving nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (TP=1, MTP n=3, `--cudagraph-capture-sizes 4 8 16`). On `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`v0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5`), engine init fails during CUDA graph capture, after 2 of the 3 sizes:

```
File ".../vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py", line 498, in _topk
RuntimeError: launch_cooperative_cluster, /workspace/csrc/cooperative_topk.cu:48, cooperative_topk launch failed: a kernel launch error has occurred due to cluster misconfiguration
```

We applied this PR's one-line change to the installed `qsa_indexer.py` and reran on Thor. Startup and CUDA graph capture complete, and a short serving benchmark finishes: about 16 output tok/s at concurrency 1 with ISL 2000 / OSL 128. That run used v0.33.0rc1.dev320+g335dd77b0 and also a downstream build on an earlier main.


`_topk` on current main still excludes only family 120, so this gate is still needed. #56084 makes the same change but needs a rebase, so could this one be reviewed? cc @gau-nernst, who okayed the change on #56084.

_Drafted with Claude Code._

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

`SparseAttnIndexer` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py` has the same `_cooperative_capable` gate on main (capability 90 and not family 120), so DeepSeek sparse indexer models should hit the same launch failure on Thor. #56084 covers both call sites. Should this PR pick up that hunk too, so #56084 can be closed?

         logits.shape[0] <= 64
         and logits.stride(0) % 4 == 0
         and current_platform.has_device_capability(90)
+        and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(110)

nodes.body: IIUC the launch failure comes from `supports_cluster16 = get_device_prop()->major >= 10` in `csrc/cooperative_topk.cu`, which picks the 16-block cluster on SM110 and SM12x for `num_rows <= 4`, while the 8/4/2 cluster paths fit there. Would gating that on `major == 10` instead fix every caller and keep the cooperative kernel on Thor? Fine as a follow up if the Python gate is the quicker fix.

nodes.body: Good catch, thank you. Generally, DeepSeek models are too big to run on a single Thor, but this may be relevant for multi-Thor setups. Adding this now.
